headline: Measure maximum simultaneous meetings with an end-time heap
statement: Given positive-length meeting intervals [start, end), return the minimum rooms needed to host them all. A room ending at time t can host another meeting starting at t.
intuition: Process meetings by their start times. Keep the end times of meetings still in progress in a min-heap. Before adding a meeting, remove every meeting that has ended. The largest number of simultaneous meetings is the number of rooms required.
approach: Before inserting a meeting, pop all end times at or before its start.
Push its end time and update the peak active count.
correctness: After removing finished entries and adding the current meeting, the heap contains exactly the meetings active at its start. Its size is therefore a lower bound on room capacity. Reusing ended rooms realizes that capacity, so the maximum observed size is both necessary and sufficient.
bruteForce: Compare each start with every interval to count its simultaneous meetings, taking quadratic time.

complexity.explanation: Sorting dominates; each end time is pushed and popped once.

pitfalls: End equal to start is reusable; use <=.
Return the peak size, not the heap size after the final meeting.
Remove all completed meetings, not just one when counting active occupancy.
